elements.reason: The panel's labelled selects and hand-off buttons, each applied at once: a form would ask for a submit button it never has (HTML_CodeSniffer H32.2), and a fieldset for a legend the panel's heading already gives.
The grid worst_groups.js fills with its titled n-gram cards (sections), itself inside the titled n-gram section: a layout box, no element means a grid of cards.
The panel grid's three columns, which stack or sit side by side with its width; layout only, without a heading to make each a section.
The open panel's layout grid of its columns and its n-gram section; a pure layout box with no meaning of its own.
The decorative ▲ or ▼ beside a change, aria-hidden and said in words by the cell's screen-reader text; no element carries a decorative glyph.
Text for screen readers only (the verdict in words, a finger's ideal load), visually hidden; it is inline text inside a cell, with no meaning beyond the words.
The coloured fill of a finger's load bar inside its aria-hidden track; a purely visual shape (a meter cannot draw the ideal-load mark across it).
The ideal-load mark drawn across a finger's bar, inside its aria-hidden track; a positioned visual line, said in words in the value's cell.
The decorative ↔, → and ↺ between the keys of a swap or a cycle, coloured, inside the aria-hidden drawing that the cycle's sentence and the « Apply » name say in words.
The decorative ▲ of a swap's gain, aria-hidden and said in words by the gain's screen-reader text; no element carries a decorative glyph.
Text for screen readers only (a cycle's moves, the gain's verdict in words), visually hidden; inline words with no meaning of their own.
The named group (role group) of the PNG and SVG save buttons and their status, a button row; a fieldset's legend would leave the row's flex layout.
The group's visible caption, aria-hidden since the group carries the same name; a legend needs a fieldset and a label names one control, not a group of buttons.
The aria-hidden bar of an n-gram's share inside its button, a purely visual shape; the share is said in the button's text and name.
The tablist container: no HTML element carries the tablist role, its tabs are native buttons with role tab.
A layout grid putting the corpus card beside the options card; each card is a section, the wrapper means nothing.

A field grouping a label, its control and a note paragraph (or the label line with its « i »): a p cannot hold a p, so the group is a div. The text mode field: its label, its select and the note paragraph under them; a p cannot hold that note.
Lays the corpus file button beside its formats, name and error paragraphs; a p cannot hold them and the group has no heading of its own.
A two-column layout grid of the keyboard and format fields, which are already grouped by their section.
A wrapping row laying out the three filter labels of the layout list; the list's section and summary already name it.
The scrolling box of the layout list's letter groups (each a heading and a ul); it only clips and scrolls them.
A layout grid of the weight group sections, each named by its own heading; the grid itself means nothing.
A layout grid putting the hands picture beside the list of ideal loads it draws.
The overview's layout grid of its figure sections, side by side when the width holds them.
Lays a checkbox, its help paragraph and the CSV button on one wrapping line; a p cannot hold the help paragraph.
A layout grid putting the n-gram board beside its list, both inside their figure section.

The hidden board drawing: a box of absolutely positioned key caps that repeats the n-gram list, no element draws a board. The heatmap board: a scaled box of absolutely positioned key caps; each key is a named image, the box only places them. A heat card's board: a scaled box of absolutely positioned key caps, each a named image; no element draws a board.
The mount point board/worst_groups.js fills with its own n-gram list markup; it adds no meaning of its own.
A legend's colour sample, aria-hidden: a drawn box beside the entry's words, which say what it stands for.
A layout grid of the tab's metric figures, each a section named by its heading.
The mount point stackedFigure() redraws with the figure's legend, bar table, note and folded table, inside its named section.
The mount point stackedFigure() redraws with the figure's legend, bar table, note and folded table, inside its named section.
A layout grid of the side-by-side heat cards, each a section named by its heading.
A layout grid of the details' figure sections, two or three columns where the width holds them.
The mount point of the image buttons group that board/board_image.js builds for the heatmap.
The box the Pareto tab redraws its scatter plot or its spread into (a named svg image), keeping it at a readable width; the table under them says every point in words.
The mount point the trace tab refills with its events table and one titled section per traced layout; it adds no meaning of its own.
A character of the trace strip above its keys, inside the aria-hidden strip that the keystroke table repeats in words.
The legend of a key cap of the trace strip, inside the aria-hidden strip that the keystroke table repeats in words.
The finger printed under a key cap of the trace strip (so its colour is never the only cue), inside the aria-hidden strip that the keystroke table repeats in words.

A drawn bar, absolutely positioned in its aria-hidden track cell; the row's cells say its value. A key of the trace strip (its finger-coloured cap holding the key's legend and its finger), inside the aria-hidden strip that the keystroke table repeats in words.
One leader tile of the dl: HTML allows only a div to wrap a dt and its dd, and the tile needs that box for its frame.
Keeps a column header's sort button and its « i » together on the header's last line; no phrasing element groups two controls.
A relative cell's drawn mark (▲ ▼ =), aria-hidden; the words beside it in la-sr-only say the verdict.
Words read by assistive technology only (a cell's unit or verdict); no element is visually hidden text.
A drawn bar or bar part, absolutely positioned in its aria-hidden track cell; the row's cells say its value.
A drawn mark (the ideal load, the middle) positioned in an aria-hidden track; the value cell says it in words.
The heat scale's drawn ramp, aria-hidden, between its two ends written as text.
A positioned key cap of the heat board, a named image (role img, its value and place in its name); no element is a key cap.
Keeps a swatch with its words as one item of the legend's flex line (its own 6 px gap); no phrasing element means a legend entry.
A verdict's drawn mark (▲ ▼ =), aria-hidden, before the words that say it.
The board on which the key buttons are absolutely positioned, sized by the script; a drawing surface with no meaning of its own (the keys carry the names).
The visible button face of the import label (the native file input's own words stay hidden): the label element is the control's name, the face is only its look.
Groups the popover's explanation paragraphs, replaced together on each opening; it is no section (no heading of its own) and no other element means a run of paragraphs.
The flex row that wraps the list of open layouts (display: contents) and its « + » button together, so « + » follows the last tab on its line; it means nothing itself.
A note (role=note) holding its paragraph and its two convert buttons; HTML has no note element, and a section would need a heading this notice does not have.
The column that stacks the page's current question, message, note and lost-features list with their own gap, hidden while empty; each child carries its own meaning.
The CSS grid of the details' labelled fields; the fields commit on change, so a form element (whose Enter submits) would be wrong, and the grid has no legend.
The wrapping flex row of the layer bar's heading, its two tab lists and its two buttons; a block holding a heading and tab lists, no element carries that grouping.
The containers of the layer tab lists (role=tablist: the four levels and the other layers), which HTML has no element for.
The auto-fit CSS grid placing the layers tool's two sections side by side; each section has its heading.
The container of the secondary tools' tabs (role=tablist), which HTML has no element for.
The drawn keyboard: a named group (role=group) of key buttons positioned in key units by CSS variables, walked with the arrow keys; no element is a two-dimensional set of positioned controls.
The legend of a positioned key cap (.le-legend), centred and shrunk to fit inside the key button by fitLegends; plain text inside a button, no element carries it.
The printed name (Tab, Shift) on a positioned key cap, laid out under its legend inside the key button; plain text inside a button.
The sideways scroll box and size container (container-type) of the drawn board; purely a layout box around the key group.
The slot whose fields change with the mapping kind chosen (a text field with its palette details, or a drop-down); it holds block content, so no paragraph, and it has no legend of its own.
The box a name search refills with its count paragraph and its list of characters; it means nothing beyond its two children.
The bordered block of the simple shortcut case: its labelled drop-down, its pick button and its note paragraph; block content without a heading or a legend.
The drawn input bar of « Try »: a transparent field laid over the output it fills, and the clear button; a visual frame around native controls.
A printed key cap (print only, aria-hidden), a CSS grid of its level legends.
One level's legend placed in a grid cell of a printed key cap (print only, aria-hidden).
The CSS grid of the board column, the key inspector and the host's side panel, whose columns follow the editor's width.
The first column of the workspace grid, stacking the board's section and the preview's section.
The persistent slot a host fills with its own panel (the Studio's analysis, itself a named section); the slot only places it in the grid.
The grid that places the four step sections in two columns on a wide screen; it groups nothing a reader needs, and an ol would announce a list around sections that already carry numbered headings.
The grid that sets the three labelled selects side by side; each field is a p with its label, and the row itself has no meaning (a fieldset would need a legend the step heading already gives).
The tablist container of the ARIA tabs pattern (role=tablist, named by its h3); its tabs are native buttons with a roving tabindex and the arrow, Home and End keys, and no HTML element is a tab list.
The box a board wider than a phone scrolls in (overflow-x), around the board; a purely visual frame.

The toolbar container (role=toolbar, named by its tab) of the absolutely positioned key buttons; one tab stop, the arrow keys move between keys. No element lays out keys on a keyboard's geometry. The toolbar container (role=toolbar, named by its tab) of the absolutely positioned QWERTY key buttons; one tab stop, the arrow keys move between keys. The toolbar container (role=toolbar, named by its tab) of the absolutely positioned zone key buttons; one tab stop, the arrow keys move between keys. The positioning frame of the start layout's drawn key caps, inside a figure with its caption; the table under the boards is their text alternative. The positioning frame of the best layout's drawn key caps, inside a figure with its caption; the table under the boards is their text alternative.
A wrapping row of native preset buttons; it adds no meaning to them (menu would announce a list). A wrapping row of native buttons (and the zone's labelled select); it adds no meaning to them.
The grid of the five budget fields inside their details, whose summary names the group; each field is a p with its label.

The group of one dt and its dd inside the score dl, the one wrapper HTML allows there, drawn as a tile. The dt and dd group of the score change inside the score dl (the one wrapper HTML allows there), drawn as a tile coloured by the change's sign.
The positioning frame of the chart's hidden svg and its pointer tip, inside the figure; purely visual.
The box a table wider than a phone scrolls in (overflow-x), around a real table; a purely visual frame.
The grid that sets the start and best boards' two figures side by side; it adds no meaning.
The grid that sets the two halves of the metrics table side by side under their h3; it adds no meaning.
The flex column the library card's verdict, best layout section, heading, list and legend are drawn into once the scan ends; the section around it carries the heading.
The decorative glyph of the verdict, hidden from assistive technology, so the verdict is not told by colour alone; its words follow.
The decorative arrow of a score gap, hidden from assistive technology; the gap's words follow it.
A wrapping row of a layout's two native « Compare » and « Edit » buttons; it adds no meaning to them.
A decorative conic ring hidden from assistive technology (aria-hidden); the same percentage is said in words beside it, and a meter cannot be drawn as a ring.
The number drawn in the decorative ring, hidden with it; the same value is said in words beside it.
The flex column of the best layout's facts beside its gauge, inside its section, so the two wrap on a phone; it adds no meaning.
The decorative track of a layout's two similarity bars, hidden from assistive technology; the values are said in words under it.
A purely visual bar inside the hidden track, its width the value said in words under it.
The decorative colour chip beside each legend entry's words, hidden from assistive technology.
The flex row that keeps the thumb keys switch's label and its separate « i » button on one line; a button cannot sit inside the label.
The decorative changed or unchanged glyph of a table row, hidden from assistive technology; its words follow.
The decorative better or worse triangle of a metric change, hidden from assistive technology; the visually hidden words beside it say the same.
Words for assistive technology only (better or worse) beside the triangle; no element hides text visually while keeping it read.
The decorative rank badge, hidden from assistive technology; the ordered list gives each layout its rank.
A decorative bar of the gain over the start, hidden from assistive technology; the gain is said in the facts line.
